lines.li: [us] How do you find our food?
[them,their:tribal] It fills the belly, and nobody at your table eats alone.
[them,their:empire] Plain, though I have eaten worse at court and paid more for it.
[them] Plain and filling, which is what a guest should hope for.
[us] Tell {COOK}, it'll be welcome.
[us] I'll pass that on to the kitchen.
[them] Your people are all up before the light.
[us] The work doesn't wait for anyone.
[them,their:empire] At court nobody rises before noon who can help it.
[them] At home only the bakers keep hours like these.
[us] You're up late.
[them] I write my letters home at night, while it's quiet.
[us] Then I won't keep you from it.
[them] Your people work straight through the rain.
[us] It's that or not eat.
[them] I'll put that in my letter, it says more than I could.
[them] Nobody at home warned me how cold it gets here.
[us,lowtech] Sit nearer the fire, nobody will mind.
[us] There are spare blankets, you only have to ask.
[them] This heat must be easier on people born to it.
[us] Nobody born here finds it easy.
[them] That's a comfort, in a way.
[them] Where I come from, snow is something in children's stories.
[us] And now?
[them] Now I'll have a story of my own to bring home.
[them] I'll be writing home about your council's new decree.
[us] Don't make it sound worse than it is.
[them] I'll write it the way I heard it at your table.
[them] My people will want to hear how your colony holds its elections.
[us] By vote, and a lot of arguing beforehand.
[them,their:tribal] Among us the elders choose, and nobody counts hands.
[them,their:empire] At court such things are settled by rank, not by a show of hands.
[them] The arguing is the part they'll want to hear about.
[them] I kept indoors during the raid, as your people asked.
[us] That was the safest place for you.
[them,their:tribal] My people will hear how your colony keeps a guest-friend in a raid.
[them] I'll write home about it, all of it.
[them] I'm sorry about {DEAD}.
[us] Thank you.
[them] I'll tell my people what {DEAD} was to you, as well as I understood it.
[them] A child born while I'm here, my people will take that as a good sign.
[us] We'll take any good sign we're given.
[them] Your children follow me about as if I were a traveling show.
[us] They've never had a guest stay so long.
[them] I've started telling them stories, so I suppose I am one now.
[them] I've been learning the names of your animals.
[us] All of them?
[them] Most of them, and a few of their tempers.
[them] Your stores look thin, and I don't want to eat more than my share.
[us] A guest eats at our table, that's settled.
[them] Then I'll write home that your people share even when it's hard.
[them] Your storerooms are fuller than I expected.
[us] We plan ahead.
[them] My people will be glad to hear it, and a few will be jealous.
[them] I didn't expect a guest's walk to take me past your cells.
[us] Every colony has its prisoners.
[them] And every guest writes home about them, so be ready for that.
[them] I'm a guest at your table while one of my own people sits in your cells.
[us] It's an odd season for both of us.
[them] Odd is a kind word for it, and my people will want a better one.
[them,them:married] I miss {THEIRSPOUSE} more than I thought I would.
[them,them:parent] I miss {THEIRCHILD} more than I thought I would.
[them] I miss home more than I thought I would.
[us] A season is a long time to be away.
[them] It is, but the letters help.
[us] Why did your people choose you to come here?
[them,their:tribal] I've sat by more strange fires than anyone in my camp.
[them,their:medieval] I can read, write and keep my temper, which is rarer than it sounds.
[them,their:industrial] I speak plainly and I don't get homesick, or so I told them.
[them,their:empire] My house was asked for someone of rank, and I was the one it could spare.
[them,their:spacer] My record matched the posting better than anyone else's.
[them] Someone had to come, and I was the one who said yes.
[us] We're glad it was you.
[them] Where I come from a guest is expected to help, and sitting idle feels wrong.
[us] Here a guest only has to be a guest.
[them] I'm finding that harder than any work.
[them] At home the guest-friend sits nearest the fire, and nobody asks them to fetch wood.
[us] Nobody here will ask you to fetch wood either.
[them] I've noticed, and I'm not sure I like it.
[them] I came with letters of credence, and nobody here knew what to do with them.
[us] We read them, at least.
[them] That's more than some courts manage.
[them] Mind if I take notes while we talk?
[us] What for?
[them] My people want to know how a place like this runs, from the people who run it.
[them] My report home has a section on your colony's habits.
[us] Which habits?
[them] All of them, so it's a long section.
[them] At court even a junior envoy keeps a room of their own.
[us] Out here a room of your own is a luxury.
[them] Then I will mention the luxury in my letters, if your colony finds me one.
[them] I'm told your best cook is {COOK}.
[us] That's fair to say.
[them] Then a fine meal before my next letter home would not go unmentioned.
[them] I've been watching how your people keep {OURFAITH}.
[us] Does it seem strange to you?
[them] Less strange than I expected, and I'll say so in my letters.
[them] You're the colony's speaker, so I should be careful with you.
[us] You can be honest with me.
[them] Among my people, honest and careful aren't the same thing.
[us] How are you feeling?
[them] Better than I look, and I'll leave the worst of it out of my letter.
[them] I'm here because my people sent me, let's leave it at that.
[us] Then we'll try to make the season bearable.
[them] Every slight I get here goes into my next letter home.
[us] Then write it fairly, and the good with it.
[them] I'll be sorry to leave when the season's done.
[us] We'll be sorry to see you go.
[them] Will you write to me, when I'm home?
[us] If someone can carry it, yes.
[them] Then I'll keep an eye on the road.
[them] Is {ENVOY} keeping well?
[us] Well enough, and eating at our table every day.
[them] I'll say so at home, people there worry.
[them] I hope you treat {ENVOY} better than you treat most visitors.
[us] We treat {ENVOY} as a guest, and a guest is what they are.
[us] Do you know {ENVOY} well?
[them] Everyone at home knows {ENVOY}, it's that kind of place.
[us] Then everyone must be reading the letters.
[them] Out loud, in the evenings, with arguments about what each line means.
[us] How is {OURENVOY} getting on at your town?
[them,their:tribal] They sit with the elders most evenings and ask about everything.
[them,their:medieval] They're at the hall most days, listening more than they talk.
[them,their:hightech] They've learned the town faster than some who were born there.
[them] Well, as far as I can tell.
[us] Good, we miss them here.
[them] {OURENVOY} writes home often, I've seen the letters go.
[us] They tell us what goes on at your town.
[them] I hope they leave out the gossip.
[us] They don't, which is half of why we read them.
[us] Is {OURENVOY} eating well among your people?
[them,their:tribal] They eat what we eat, and they've stopped asking what it is.
[them] They eat at our tables like anyone else.
[us] Good, we only packed them enough for the road.
[them] Some at home wonder what {OURENVOY} is really there for.
[us] To know your people better, nothing else.
[them] My people have grown fond of {OURENVOY}.
[us] I'm glad to hear it.
[them] Don't be surprised if {OURENVOY} comes home with a few of our habits.
[them] The envoy we sent you came home with nothing but good to say.
[us] We tried to make them welcome.
[them,their:tribal] It worked, and the elders have heard every word of it.
[them] It worked, they've told it to anyone who'll listen.
[them] Our envoy's report on your household was read at court, and favorably.
[us] We're glad to hear it.
[them] You should be, the court is not easily pleased.
[them] Someone of ours came home from your colony feeling slighted.
[us] That was never what we meant.
